# dsh-trust-suite
**The deterministic trust layer for DeepSeek Harness — nine guards, one dashboard, one command.**
为 DeepSeek Harness 打造的确定性信任层：九个守卫 + 一块人话面板，一条命令全装上。
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Install · The nine guards · Honest scope · FAQ
Nine deterministic guards watch what a DSH agent **reads, writes, executes, spends, and remembers**
— plus a plain-language dashboard and a guardian pet that makes the state visible at a glance. Every
decision is made by pure rule engines: **zero LLM calls in the trust path**, ~140 unit tests, verif
ied against real DSH sessions.
## The nine guards

| dsh-read-guard | what the agent **reads** | `tools/post-execute` | wrap (default) · observe · bloc

| dsh-egre

ss-gate | where data **goes** | `tools/pre-execute` | web: deny · shell: observe |
| dsh-attest-chai

n | what **happened** (evidence) | `tools/result` | sign + hash chain |
| dsh-mcp-test | which **too

ls exist** | `tools/change` | baseline diff |
| dsh-prompt-drift | the **system prompt** | `system-p

rompt/assemble` | baseline diff |

Plus two consumers of the same event stream:
- **dsh-trust-panel** — a sidebar dashboard that translates the nine channels into plain language, b

ilingual (zh/en), with a status light and acknowledge flow.

## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That single bundle installs all nine guards plus the dashboard. Prefer git checkouts? `./install.sh
web` from this repo does the same from GitHub sources (everything ships prebuilt `lib/`, no `allowBu
ilds` approval needed). Individual guards are also installable on their own.
## Honest scope

> [!WARNING]
> **This is a policy-check and audit toolset, not a sandbox.** The guards make determin
istic decisions at DSH's plugin hook points; they are not OS-level network controls, filesystem perm
issions, or a semantic guarantee that "the model was never influenced". Hard boundaries belong to th
e host sandbox, system permissions, or a proxy — layer this suite *on top of* those, not instead of
t sandbox, system permissions, or a proxy — layer this suite *on top of* those, not instead of them.
What each guard actually does, stated plainly:
- **Detect** (report + ledger): mcp-test, prompt-drift, freeze, compaction-guard, janitor flag drift

and leftovers — they do not block anything.
- **Enforce before the fact**: pr-gate denies out-of-sc
ope file writes; egress-gate denies non-allowlisted web destinations (shell fetches are observe-only

by default).
- **Mutate results**: read-guard wraps flagged content in a quarantine envelope (defau
lt) or blocks it — in wrap mode the original text is still in context, explicitly marked untrusted.
- **Record**: attest-chain appends a signed, hash-chained evidence record per tool result.
Known boundaries are documented per guard in each repo's README — coverage limits, default-off modes
, and trust-on-first-use for baselines.
## FAQ
**Does this call any LLM?** No. Every decision is a pure rule engine — same input, same verdict, aud
this call any LLM?** No. Every decision is a pure rule engine — same input, same verdict, auditable.
**Can I install just one guard?** Yes. Every guard is an independent npm package; the suite is only
a convenience bundle. dsh-trust-panel even works standalone — its read/egress engines ship inside th
ndle. dsh-trust-panel even works standalone — its read/egress engines ship inside the panel package.
**Does read-guard delete or rewrite the original file?** Never. It only changes what reaches the mod
el's context, and only for high-severity findings in wrap/block mode.
**Windows?** Yes — CI runs Windows + Linux on Node 20/22/24 for every guard.
**Exact supported set** (as verified): Node ≥ 20 · npm ≥ 11.15 (staged publishing route) · DSH 0.2.x
source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2 with host packages on the 0.1.2-rc.1 line · dsh plugin add installs v
ia the official profile flow (pnpm). Plain-npm installs of the suite depend on the registry peer gra
ph resolving cleanly — dsh-prompt-drift ≥ 0.1.1 carries the peer fix that makes that resolve.
